newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian cyclone Justin remains off coast.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian cyclone Justin remains off coast.

text.p: Cyclone Justin remained of diminished intensity and was expected to be almost stationary off the Queensland coast over the next 24 hours, Australia's weather bureau said.
The cyclone was 600 km northeast of Bowen on Thursday morning and expected to move only slowly in the next 24 hours, an official with the bureau's cyclone warning centre in Brisbane said.
It was expected to remain well off the coast, he said.
As a category one storm it posed no threat, although the bureau would maintain a close watch on it, he said.
The coastal area between Bowen and Mackay had experienced especially strong seas, which were now easing, he said.
However, strong wind warnings remained, with winds expected to cover an increased area of the coast, he said.
Justin had brought no sign of increased rainfall over Queensland, he said.
Justin closed Queensland coal export ports for the past four days, delaying the export of almost one million tonnes of coal.
Sugar industry leaders have warned that if the cyclone hit Australia's sugar crop it could cause world prices to jump.
Australia is the world's largest exporter of coal and one of the world's largest exporters of sugar. Queensland is the main producing state for both goods.
The cyclone has also whipped up high winds in Papua New Guinea to the north.
